status_summary: HHS and USDA released the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines in January 2026 (White House briefing dated 2026-01-07). According to the supplemental scientific foundation report, the 2025 advisory committee report was not used as the basis; that report was written by external scientists with NIH-coordinated peer review. The guidelines document is about ten pages, addresses protein, full-fat dairy, limits on highly processed foods and added sugar, and does not address environmental sustainability. This matches the Mandate's minimum reform option on keeping the guidelines focused on nutrition; whether the new process meets the Mandate's transparency standard is not assessed here. Repeal and codification in law were not pursued in anything reviewed. On 2026-08-19 the Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine sued USDA and HHS in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, alleging that the agencies relied on an outside panel formed without the transparency and oversight required by the Federal Advisory Committee Act (one law-firm summary adds the Administrative Procedure Act) and asking the court to order withdrawal of the 2025-2030 guidelines; no ruling or agency response was reported. The suit disputes the transparency of the new process, which the Mandate asked to improve.

timeline.event: HHS and USDA announce the Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2025-2030 (White House briefing dated 2026-01-07 per the program website); the guidelines are signed by the HHS and USDA Secretaries.

The guidelines document is published: a roughly ten-page text that prioritizes protein and whole foods, recommends full-fat dairy without added sugar, and advises limiting highly processed foods and added sugar; it does not discuss environmental sustainability.

The supplemental Scientific Foundation report and appendices are posted (the appendices file name carries the date 1.28.26; the report states the 2025 advisory committee report was not used as the basis).

The Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine filed suit against USDA and HHS in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, alleging violations of the Federal Advisory Committee Act in the process used for the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines and seeking their withdrawal; no ruling was reported.

H.R. 8578, the FRESH Act, is introduced and referred to the House Committee on Agriculture; per a tracker summary it would lock in the 2025-2030 guidelines and require congressional approval of future editions (a member press release is dated 2026-04-30).
